context: The prompt requests to move the Technical Design functionality out of the Workdir tab into a standalone tab in the Web UI navigation, similar to how Requirements has its own dedicated section. Currently, Technical Design is only accessible via a quick link button within the Workdir section, which makes it less discoverable and doesn't provide the same level of prominence as Requirements.

questions.question-text: Where should the new Technical Design navigation item be positioned in the main menu?

options.label: Between 'Requirements' and 'Help'
options.pros: Keeps all specification-related sections (Requirements, Technical Design) together; natural flow from Requirements to Technical Design
options.cons: Changes existing navigation order that users may be familiar with

options.label: Between 'Workdir' and 'Requirements'
options.pros: Groups all specification/document sections together; maintains Requirements near the end; logical progression from workspace to specifications
options.cons: May interrupt the flow between Workdir and Requirements that some users expect

options.label: At the end, after 'Help'
options.pros: Doesn't disturb existing navigation order; easy to add without affecting current menu
options.cons: Less discoverable; separates it from Requirements which is related content

questions.recommendation-rationale: Placing Technical Design between Requirements and Help creates a logical grouping of specification-related sections. Since Requirements and Technical Design are both part of the specifications folder and serve similar purposes (defining what to build), keeping them adjacent improves discoverability and provides a better user experience.

questions.question-text: Should the Technical Design section allow editing the JSON file directly as text, or provide an interactive form-based interface?

options.label: Direct JSON text editor (like Requirements uses for markdown)
options.pros: Simple to implement; consistent with how Requirements section works; allows full control and copy/paste; familiar pattern
options.cons: Requires understanding of JSON syntax; error-prone; no validation; less user-friendly for non-technical users

options.label: Interactive form-based interface driven by configuration
options.pros: User-friendly; prevents syntax errors; can provide validation; better UX for non-technical users; already mentioned in UR-0018
options.cons: More complex to implement; requires configuration-driven form logic; may be overkill if technical-design.json is currently empty

options.label: Both options: toggle between JSON editor and form view
options.pros: Maximum flexibility; caters to both technical and non-technical users; allows experts to edit directly while beginners use forms
options.cons: Most complex to implement; requires synchronization between views; may confuse users about which view to use

questions.recommendation-rationale: For the initial implementation, a direct JSON text editor is recommended because: (1) it's simpler to implement and consistent with the existing Requirements section pattern, (2) the technical-design.json file is currently empty so there's no immediate need for complex form logic, and (3) UR-0018 mentions form-based editing but doesn't require it for this specific prompt. The form-based interface can be added in a future enhancement when the technical design schema is better defined.

questions.question-text: What icon should be used for the Technical Design navigation menu item?

options.label: bi-diagram-3 (diagram/architecture icon)
options.pros: Represents technical architecture and design well; visually distinct from other menu items; commonly associated with technical design
options.cons: May be less familiar to some users

options.label: bi-file-earmark-code (code document icon)
options.pros: Indicates technical/code-related content; consistent with document-style icons used elsewhere
options.cons: Similar to other file-based icons; may not specifically convey 'design' concept

options.label: bi-gear-wide-connected (interconnected gears)
options.pros: Represents system design and architecture; shows interconnected components; technical feel
options.cons: May be confused with settings or configuration

options.label: bi-file-earmark-text (generic document icon, same as Requirements)
options.pros: Consistent with Requirements section; simple and familiar
options.cons: Identical to Requirements icon; doesn't distinguish Technical Design from Requirements visually

questions.recommendation-rationale: The bi-diagram-3 icon best represents technical design and architecture concepts. It's visually distinct from the bi-file-text icon used for Requirements, helping users quickly distinguish between the two specification-related sections. The diagram/architecture metaphor aligns well with what users expect from a technical design section.

questions.question-text: Should the quick link button in the Workdir section be removed after creating the standalone Technical Design tab?

options.label: Yes, remove it completely
options.pros: Eliminates redundancy; cleaner UI; encourages users to use the main navigation; single source of truth
options.cons: Users who frequently work in Workdir may find it less convenient; removes quick access option

options.label: No, keep it as a convenience shortcut
options.pros: Provides quick access for users working in Workdir; maintains backward compatibility; no functionality removed
options.cons: Redundant; may confuse users about which way to access Technical Design; clutters Workdir interface

options.label: Keep it but change it to a navigation link instead of loading in place
options.pros: Provides convenience without redundancy; clear that it navigates to the dedicated section; maintains discoverability
options.cons: Requires JavaScript to switch sections; slightly more complex implementation

questions.recommendation-rationale: Removing the quick link button eliminates redundancy and provides a cleaner, more consistent user experience. With Technical Design having its own dedicated navigation tab, users will have a clear, discoverable way to access it. This follows the same pattern as Requirements, which doesn't have a quick link button in Workdir. Maintaining a single access point reduces confusion and keeps the UI focused.

questions.question-text: What background color should be used for the Technical Design section header?

options.label: bg-warning (yellow/orange) to distinguish from other sections
options.pros: Visually distinct from existing sections; creates clear visual separation; yellow often represents design/planning
options.cons: Warning color may imply caution or problems; may not match overall color scheme

options.label: bg-info (blue) to match a technical/informational theme
options.pros: Same as Requirements, showing they are related specification documents; consistent color palette; professional appearance
options.cons: Identical to Requirements; doesn't provide visual distinction between the two specification sections

options.label: bg-secondary (gray) for a neutral technical appearance
options.pros: Neutral and professional; distinguishes from both Requirements (blue) and other sections
options.cons: May appear less prominent; gray is used for Help section which is less critical

options.label: bg-primary (blue, same as navbar) for consistency
options.pros: Matches primary brand color; consistent with overall design
options.cons: Same as Prompts History; doesn't create distinction for this important section

questions.recommendation-rationale: Using bg-info (blue) maintains consistency with the Requirements section and reinforces that both are specification-related documents. This visual similarity helps users understand they serve related purposes (defining the system) while the different icons and labels keep them distinguishable. The blue color also conveys professionalism and information, which is appropriate for technical design content.
